question: Does exact high-x-bit indexing reduce full-table search work while preserving full recovery certificates, and what bounded frontier completes at48/52/56/58/60bits on one RTXPRO6000?

claims.text: Every reported recovery is independently replayed from a serialized certificate and corrupted-scalar certificates are rejected.
Largest complete rung is an observed bounded frontier for these fixtures and two seeds, not a mathematical maximum or certified time advantage.

arms.description: Full GPU-backed reduction with high-x-bit prefix lookup index
Identical indexed GPU binaries and inputs, second invocation
Same driver/service source with ER_QUERY_BINARY_REFERENCE to retain full-table binary search,48/52bits only

positive.not_applicable_reason: All successful public-input recoveries must satisfy scalar multiplication and complete independent certificate replay; existing tiny known-answer reduction controls run first.

negative.not_applicable_reason: Each successful certificate is copied with scalar incremented modulo r; a fresh verifier must reject with exit1, not timeout. Invalid curves/order witnesses are tested before measurement.

factors.name: source_and_build
factors.how: One pinned source, recorded hashes; u/x identical; b differs only ER_QUERY_BINARY_REFERENCE. Both services log table row counts and admission bytes.

factors.name: inputs
factors.value: Deterministic PARI48/52/56/58/60-bit fixtures; public target first even-y lift from x=1009*seed, seeds101/202.48/52/56 fixture rule identical to v3.
factors.how: No target scalar is generated or supplied. Curve order is checked with prime torsion witness and unique Hasse multiple before solving.

factors.name: host
factors.how: Same full RTX PRO6000 and pod for all rows. Record device identity, GPU state, CPU affinity and CPUinfo; shared host earns only L0.

factors.name: memory_layout
factors.how: Fresh processes sample ASLR; same explicit caps and launch geometry. Eight slots and tau=2*ceil(r^(1/8))+2 fixed for all arms.

factors.name: order
factors.how: Increasing resource ladder.48/52seed101 b/u/x,seed202 x/u/b;56/58/60seed101 u/x,seed202 x/u. Complete current rung then stop after any timeout/limit.

factors.name: analyst
factors.how: Frozen Rust analyzer validates complete attempted rungs and labels, preserves failures, and plots all rows. No inferential timing analysis.

comparisons.threshold: Every reported succeeded execution has one independently replayed recovery and rejected corrupt scalar.

randomization.arm_order_reason: Increasing resource ladder with reversed baseline/candidate/AA order by seed; complete current rung then stop after first incomplete rung.

seed_derivation.note: Exactly101 and202 for each arm and rung; target-coordinate start1009*seed; solver uses same seed for hash/trial RNG.

instance_sampling.rule: First nonsingular prime-order a=-3 curve at precprime(2^bits),b1..8192,bits48/52/56/58/60; first liftable generatorx1..1000. PARI cardinality independently certified by driver. Same fixed public-target rule asv3.

blinding.how: Descriptive frontier accounting; no masked or inferential timing claim.

power.note: Exact certificate and boundary checks, not population or timing inference. Two fixed public targets per rung with A/A repeats; no significance test.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Unmeasured allocation estimate. Existing tiny correctness suite is preflight; actual ladder costs are retained. Per-solve300s, curve-generation180s, worker2400s/controller2700s.

primary.name: Independently replayed recovery
primary.definition: One iff solver succeeded, fresh verifier replay passed and corrupted-scalar replay failed; otherwise zero. Public target scalar never generated.

secondary.name: Complete execution and audit
secondary.definition: Outer native clock from target-coordinate construction through solver startup/recovery/shutdown, independent replay, negative-control replay and certificate comparisons. Includes validation overhead.

secondary.name: Cold complete recovery
secondary.definition: Outer clock from target-coordinate construction through driver startup, curve validation, service startup, bases, relation collection, elimination, in-process certificate replay, serialization and process teardown. Additional independent replay excluded and recorded separately.

record: Stage clocks and outer complete execution clock
Bound failures and unattempted higher rungs

placement.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

stopping_rules.rule: At48/52bits run2seeds times3GPU arms b/u/x. At56/58/60bits run2seeds times2indexed GPU arms u/x. Maximum24rows. Complete current rung then stop higher rungs if any timeout/limit. No post-outcome tuning or retry.
300s per solve,60s per replay,180s fixture generation,2400s worker2700s controller. Retain timeouts and limit failures as incomplete rows, not absence proofs.

invalidation_rules: Any incorrect recovery, accepted corrupt certificate, differing successful cross-arm certificate, failed sanitizer or unexpected process error invalidates the run. Explicit limits/timeouts are frontier observations, not invalidity.

decision_rule.text: Report verified executions and largest rung completed by both seeds and A/A; retain incomplete rung and record higher rungs as unattempted. No global maximum, speedup or fastest-tool conclusion.
decision_rule.threshold: every reported recovery independently replayed; all attempted rung cells accounted for
decision_rule.statistic: exact completed recovery count and descriptive per-execution stage clocks
decision_rule.interval: none; fixed public inputs and raw per-execution values

graphs: Every solver execution against field bits, including bounded failures

inadmissible: Claiming a largest possible ECDLP size from a finite timed ladder
Treating L0 times as certified speedups
Hiding unsuccessful trials or higher unattempted rungs
Claiming a tensor or subexponential backend from generic MITM
Supplying the target scalar to recovery

literature.ref: user supplied Subexponential ECDL paper, sections1.2 and3
literature.claim: Paper reduction has factor bases,relation collection,linear algebra and extraction; claimed asymptotic contraction is conditional and not practical-curve speed evidence.
Point order divides group order; Hasse interval bounds full cardinality. Exact prime torsion witness and unique multiple certify cofactor one.
ellcard returns finite-field curve cardinality; used for public fixture construction, independently certified again by driver.
Lower-bound on a sorted full-key range preserves first equal entry; prefix ranges are bounded with the same comparator. This is an engineering index, not a new decomposition algorithm.
literature.verified_by: Read NVIDIA primary implementation documentation2026-10-30; existing curve.cuh RowLess/lookup examined.
